title: Postmortem review: duplicate Acme credits (18 Feb)

transcript.text: Timeline first. At 21:40 on the 18th Acme had an outage and queued their callbacks.
They came back about 26 hours later and we credited 41 payouts twice, because the keys had expired.
Alerting caught it from the ledger imbalance check about 40 minutes later.
We reversed all 41 the same morning. I'd like to revisit the key TTL properly at the architecture review rather than patch it today.
Agreed. Action item: revisit idempotency TTL, owner Aditya.

notes: Root cause: Acme callback retries arrived after the 24h idempotency key expiry. Action: revisit TTL (owner: Aditya).

title: Payments architecture review

transcript.text: Next item is idempotency key retention. Keys expire after 24 hours right now. Pooja, you raised this after the Feb 18 duplicates?
Yes. The duplicate credits on the 18th came from Acme retries that arrived after our key had already expired.

I want to argue for 72 hours, not 48. Acme keeps retrying failed callbacks with backoff for up to 72 hours after an outage. It's in their integration annex, not in their public docs. And their weekend batch means a Friday-night failure can get retried on Monday morning.
72 hours triples the Redis footprint for keys though.
It's about 1.2 GB at current volume and we have headroom. A duplicate credit costs us far more than memory. Anything shorter than their retry window just moves the bug.
Do merchants see any difference?
No, it's invisible to them. It only changes how long we remember a request.
OK, let's go with 72 hours. Aditya, can you make the change?
Yes, I'll ship it this week.
Last thing: Deepika, the payout report export, where are we?
Merged yesterday, it goes out with Thursday's release.

notes: Decisions: idempotency key retention extended to 72h. Actions: Aditya to update the TTL in payments-api. Deepika to ship the payout report export.

title: Checkout: 3-D Secure strategy

transcript.text: Drop-off on the 3DS challenge step is 18% for tickets under ₹2,000. I want frictionless by default below that line.
We tested it with two merchants and conversion went up 6 points without a change in chargebacks.
Fine from Risk as long as fraud rules still score every payment and we can force a challenge per merchant.
On the payments side the capture flow doesn't change. We just pass the exemption flag through to the acquirer.
Let's ship it to all merchants next sprint.

notes: Decision: frictionless 3DS under ₹2,000; Risk can force challenges per merchant.

Agreed. Shared keystore, 72h TTL, a 409 with the original response for duplicates.
I can take the Kong plugin.
Sounds good from Payments.

notes: Decision: enforce Idempotency-Key at the gateway using the shared payments keystore (72h). Swati owns the plugin.
